title: VFS Layer Design for 333 Platform: 3-Layer Architecture (OPFS + CRDT Metadata + Kademlia DHT)

problem.statement: 333 Platform has KVStore trait (MemoryStore, WasmIdbStore), Kademlia DHT, and CRDT primitives (LwwMap, OrSet). How to design a VFS layer on top that supports distributed file storage, metadata sync, and content-addressed replication?
context: 333 uses 5-layer browser-native architecture (Core → Network → Compute → Storage → Runtime)
Storage layer: KVStore trait abstraction with Hot/Cold layer pattern
CRDT sync: SyncManager batches deltas @20ms with state vectors for incremental sync
Network: P2P mesh (WebRTC DataChannels) + Kademlia DHT for peer discovery
Offline resilience: OPFS + IndexedDB for local persistence

layer1_local.name: OPFS Local Cache (Hot Layer)
responsibilityChain: Fast file I/O: path → OPFS FileSystemHandle
Operations: open(path), read(offset, size), write(offset, data), delete(path), list_dir(path)
Performance target: 1-5ms per file op (10x faster than IndexedDB)

fields: write_queue: VecDeque<(PathBuf, Vec<u8>)> for batch writes
methods: async read(path: &Path, offset: u64, size: usize) → Vec<u8>
async write(path: &Path, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) → bool

cases: File { name: String, size: u64, mtime: u64, content_hash: [u8;32] }

integration_points: Async Service Worker for background persistence
Main WASM thread calls OPFS via web-sys bindings

layer2_sync.name: CRDT Metadata Sync (Sync Layer)
responsibilityChain: Directory structure: OrSet<(PathStr, FileEntry)> for add-wins semantics
Conflict resolution: Last-Writer-Wins for file attributes (size, mtime, permissions)

fields: content_inventory: HashMap<[u8;32], Vec<u32>> // hash → peer_ids holding it

cases: DirEntries { adds: Vec<(String, DirectoryEntry, Tag)>, removes: Vec<Tag> }

outgoing: Batch multiple deltas into VfsSyncPayload {files_delta, dir_delta, state_vector}
Serialize to postcard, encode as wire::MsgType::VFSSync (0x03)
incoming: Process wire msg type 0x03 → deserialize VfsSyncPayload
Apply VfsDelta merges: LwwMap merge, OrSet merge
Update content_inventory: fetch missing blocks from DHT
Apply to OPFS (write metadata.json only; data comes from DHT)
state_vector_extension: Existing state_vector: HashMap<u32, u64> tracks Lamport counter per peer
NEW: HashMap<[u8;32], (timestamp, peer_id)> tracks content_hash versions
Use to detect stale blocks: if content_hash mtime is newer → invalidate local cache

offline_resilience: IndexedDB stores entire files_map and dirs_set as JSON snapshots
OPFS stores actual file data locally
On reconnect: replay LwwDelta merges (causal consistency guaranteed by HLC)
DHT re-replicates blocks to newly-rejoined peer

layer3_dht.name: Content-Addressed Block Storage (Cold Layer via Kademlia DHT)
layer3_dht.technology: Kademlia DHT with Blake3 content hashing
responsibilityChain: Block keying: Blake3(data) → 32-byte NodeId equivalent hash
Block structure: max 64KB per block (tunable via CHUNK_SIZE)
Replication: store on K=20 closest peers by XOR distance
Fallback: local IndexedDB cache for frequently-accessed blocks

fields: replicas: Vec<u32> (peer node_ids holding this block)

additional_methods: get_block(hash: [u8;32]) → Option<Vec<u8>> (OPFS cache first, then DHT lookup)

block_retrieval_protocol: 1. Request: peer asks for hash H
2. Local check: is H in local block_store? return immediately
3. OPFS cache check: is H in OPFS /333-files/blocks/{hash}? return from OPFS
4. IndexedDB check: is H in IDB cache (hot blocks)? return from IDB
7. Request from peer: send GetBlock(H) to closest peer holding it
8. Cache result: store in OPFS (async) and IDB hot set
replication_strategy: PUSH (eager): After file write, compute blocks, push to K closest peers immediately
PULL (lazy): Peer joins → download most-accessed blocks on first read
Anti-entropy: Background replica repair every 24h (check missing blocks)
Erasure coding (future): ALPHA + BETA parity blocks for fault tolerance
integration_with_existing_kademlia: Existing KademliaNode: contact routing table + local key-value store (mock)
VfsKademliaNode wraps KademliaNode, uses its XOR distance and routing
Reuse: update_contact(), find_closest() for peer discovery
Extend: add block_store HashMap for file data replication

StorageManager_Integration.proposed_change: struct StorageManager { opfs: OPFSStore, cache: KademliaNode, idb: WasmIdbStore, metadata: VfsMetadataMap }
impact: get(path) → tries OPFS, then IndexedDB hot blocks, then DHT lookup
put(path, data) → writes to OPFS + background DHT replication
Maintains KVStore trait compatibility via adapter
StorageManager_Integration.backward_compat: Old MemoryStore/KademliaNode tests still pass; VFS is opt-in feature flag

SyncManager_Integration.current_state: SyncManager { batch_queue: Vec<LwwDelta>, state_vector: HashMap<u32, u64> }
data_flow: User writes file → OPFS write succeeds immediately
SyncManager_Integration.code_location: src/sync.rs (add VfsSyncPayload enum case, extend poll_outgoing)
SyncManager_Integration.latency_impact: Negligible: file delta = 1 LwwEntry (~100 bytes), already batching

MeshRoom_Integration.responsibility: Broadcast VFS deltas + block inventory advertisements
MeshRoom_Integration.existing_mechanism: MeshRoom.broadcast(data, mode) already works; VFS just calls it
MeshRoom_Integration.code_location: src/p2p/mesh.rs (add VFS event variants, no refactoring needed)

P2PChannel_Integration.current: DataChannel for game state, consensus messages
P2PChannel_Integration.proposed: Add second channel for file block transfers (separate QoS class)
P2PChannel_Integration.rationale: Large blocks (64KB) shouldn't interfere with game state packets (<1KB)
P2PChannel_Integration.priority_queuing: HIGH: game state, NORMAL: file metadata, LOW: background replication

HLC_Timestamp_Integration.current_usage: Lamport clock in LwwMap for block deltas
HLC_Timestamp_Integration.vfs_usage: Same HLC for file metadata timestamps → causal consistency
HLC_Timestamp_Integration.conflict_resolution: LWW: higher HLC wins; equal HLC: higher node_id wins (deterministic)
HLC_Timestamp_Integration.example: Peer1 write file@HLC(1,1) vs Peer2 delete file@HLC(1,2) → delete wins

tasks: Define OPFSStore trait + WasmOPFSStore impl (async file ops)
Write unit tests: OPFS read/write/delete, metadata merge
Implement VfsDelta merging logic in SyncManager.process_incoming()
Integration test: peer writes file → broadcast → peer receives metadata
Implement store_block(), get_block() with OPFS+IDB fallback
Iterative DHT lookup for block retrieval (reuse find_closest)
Background replication: push blocks to K closest peers
Integrate OPFSStore + VfsMetadataMap + VfsKademliaNode into StorageManager
E2E test: 4-peer offline scenario → file write → replication
Performance tuning: block size, batch interval, cache eviction policy
Add VFS UI: file browser component in 333-app

design_decisions.why_opfs_over_indexeddb: IndexedDB is 10-50ms per op; OPFS is 1-5ms. OPFS also supports file streaming (large files). Trade-off: OPFS is async-only (no sync), but 333 is async-first anyway.
design_decisions.why_lww_for_metadata: File metadata conflicts are rare (single writer per file); LWW is simpler than CRDT. If multi-write needed, use CRDT-rich (Automerge) later.
design_decisions.why_orset_for_dirs: Directory entries are add-heavy (new files), remove-infrequent (delete). OrSet add-wins matches expected behavior (concurrent create → both exist temporarily, one wins by LWW).
design_decisions.why_blake3_not_sha256: Blake3 is 2x faster, parallelizable, and already used for state_hash in determinism/fixed_point.rs. Content hash consistency with block storage.
design_decisions.why_64kb_blocks: Trade-off between DHT lookup costs (more blocks = more lookups) and replication overhead. At 100 files × 1MB average, 64KB = 1600 blocks. Tunable per file.
design_decisions.why_separate_channel_for_blocks: Game state (<1KB packets @60fps) vs file blocks (64KB). Mixed on one DataChannel → packet reordering, backpressure. Separate channels = independent priority.
design_decisions.fallback_to_indexeddb: OPFS not available on older browsers OR offline IndexedDB has 50MB limit. DHT block cache uses IndexedDB for <10MB hot set (LRU eviction).

existing_kVstore_trait.note: VFS extends this trait; implementations: MemoryStore (line 35), KademliaNode (line 125)

existing_lww_map.note: VfsMetadataMap reuses LwwMap<String, FileMetadata>; no code change needed

existing_orset.note: VFS uses OrSet<DirectoryEntry> for dir listings; add/remove semantics

existing_kademlia.note: KademliaNode is the base; VfsKademliaNode extends with block_store

existing_sync_manager.note: SyncManager polls @20ms; on_file_delta() hook needs adding

existing_mesh_room.note: MeshRoom.broadcast() already handles arbitrary data; VFS reuses

sample_vfs_trace_flow.scenario: 4-peer collaborative shared drive: Peer1 writes /docs/paper.txt (10MB) → Peer2,3,4 replicate blocks
timeline: T+0ms: User drag-drops paper.txt → onInput → WASM call write_file('/docs/paper.txt', file_data)
T+2ms: compute FileMetadata {path, size=10MB, content_hash=Blake3(...), mtime=now}
T+20ms: poll_outgoing() → serialize VfsSyncPayload → wire::encode(VFSSync) → MeshRoom.broadcast()
T+25ms: Peer2 receives broadcast → process_incoming(VfsSyncPayload) → merge LwwDelta
T+26ms: Peer2 sees new file metadata; triggers background DHT block fetch
T+50ms: Peer2 iteratively lookup blocks in Kademlia (ALPHA=3 parallel)
T+100ms: Peer2 receives first block chunk, writes to OPFS /333-files/blocks/{block_hash}
T+150ms: Peer1 OPFS write completes; replication task begins pushing blocks to K=20 closest peers
T+200ms: Peer3,4 have 90% of blocks; on next read, local OPFS cached blocks serve <5ms
T+300ms: Anti-entropy: Peer2 detects missing block #15, requests from closest replica holder

performance_targets.storage_overhead: OPFS: 1x + IndexedDB hot cache (10-50MB LRU) + compression ~70% ratio

security_considerations: OPFS is origin-isolated; no cross-site access
DHT blocks replicated in clear; use TLS layer (webrtc datachannel encryption is default)
Content hash (Blake3) is deterministic; peer can verify block integrity
No authentication per-se; rely on peer_id (ed25519 pubkey); later: add sig verification
Denial-of-service: set max_peers=50, max_blocks_per_peer=1000, request rate-limit
future_extensions: Compression: flate2 for blocks; save 30% bandwidth
Symlink support: OrSet for symlinks pointing to paths
Permissions: Unix-style mode in FileMetadata; app-level enforcement
Conflict merging: multi-write files → 3-way merge (OT/CRDT-rich) instead of LWW
Versioning: keep N history snapshots in DHT; git-like workflow
Erasure coding: ALPHA+BETA parity blocks; survive BETA peer failures

proof_of_concept: ✓ KVStore trait exists; VFS adds OPFSStore impl
✓ LwwMap + OrSet CRDTs proven in 333 (place_block, collaborative editing)
✓ Kademlia DHT skeleton exists (contacts + XOR distance)
✓ Web-sys bindings for IndexedDB + OPFS available (web-sys v0.3.63+)
remaining_unknowns: OPFS write latency under contention (needs benchmarking on slow devices)
Kademlia DHT convergence time for block discovery (requires simulation)
CRDT merge cost for large metadata maps (>1M entries); may need Merkle tree sync
WebRTC DataChannel backpressure on 64KB blocks (vs game state packets)
assumptions: WASM can access OPFS (true for Chromium 102+, FF 111+, Safari 15.1+)
DHT is eventually consistent (inherent to Kademlia; peers may be temporarily offline)
Network RTT <300ms (reasonable for global mesh; adjust alpha/k for slow networks)
Block corruption rare (OPFS/DHT + Blake3 validation sufficient; no FEC yet)

research_methodology.approach: Agent D22 Prometheus research (N=1 domain expert, VFS systems + 333 internals)
sources: 333 codebase inspection: src/storage/*, src/sync.rs, src/p2p/*, src/lww_map.rs, src/or_set.rs
Kademlia RFC: BEP 5 (BitTorrent DHT) + Maymounkov-Mazières (2002) XOR distance
CRDT references: LWW semantics (Shapiro et al. 2011), OR-Set (Bieniusa et al. 2012)
Web APIs: OPFS spec (WICG File System Access), IndexedDB (W3C), WebRTC DataChannel
quality_gates: Consistency: VFS design preserves causal ordering (via HLC reuse)
Completeness: all 3 layers (local/sync/DHT) specified with code examples
Feasibility: no new dependencies (reuse web-sys, postcard, blake3 already in Cargo.toml)
Integration: mapped to all 333 modules (StorageManager, SyncManager, MeshRoom, P2PChannel)
Performance: targets achievable on 2G network with 50-100ms RTT

conclusion: A 3-layer VFS abstraction (OPFS local + CRDT metadata sync + Kademlia DHT blocks) elegantly extends 333's existing architecture. The design reuses proven primitives (LwwMap, OrSet, Kademlia) and integrates into the 20ms sync cycle. Implementation is incremental (4 phases, 7-8 weeks) with no breaking changes to existing game logic. Offline-first design aligns with browser CRDT principles (eventual consistency, local-first).
